NgraceChangeDesignContext.Rationale:
This document is explanatory. It records the reviewed design and the reasoning behind the one behavior this bundle changes. Obligations bind only through `spec.xml` acceptance criteria and constraints; nothing here adds a requirement, and its diagrams create no silent obligation.
The ledger-backed scope audit exists to compare the tool-generated WriteEvidence record against the plan's declared `ObservedWriteScope`, so a path recorded outside the declaration is visible even when the working tree is clean at close. `C-DECLARED-WRITES` added that audit and, in the same decision, gave every path with prefix `docs/plans/` a path-class exclusion. Its rationale was local: this repository had concurrent authority edits under that prefix, and the write evidence record could not distinguish authority work from an executor's undeclared write. The spec's own Assumption named the consequence — an arbitrary edit under `docs/plans/` would not raise.
A generic product cannot ship a publisher-local privilege. `docs/plans/` is a directory name, not an ownership signal: a consumer may keep its roadmap elsewhere, or may rely on the audit to notice an undeclared write under its own roadmap directory. The audit already answers the concurrency concern correctly for every other path — declare the path in `ObservedWriteScope` and it passes; leave it undeclared and it raises. A finding states that a recorded path is outside scope; it does not infer who authored the path. Coordination belongs in declared scope and evidence boundaries, not in a tool-defined prefix. The exclusion is therefore removed, and the historical corpus is read only as history — not edited, not re-validated against current schemas.
What does not change: the porcelain working-tree audit remains a separate code (`review.scope-outside-write-scope`) that already reports changed `docs/plans/` paths; the CLI lifecycle exclusion and the exact canonical engine candidate-lock exception remain; non-lifecycle `.ngrace/` content — including undeclared edits to approved `spec.xml`/`plan.xml` — still raises; deduplication, union across attempts, `.ngrace/` archive-identity expansion, finding severity, and the missing/empty-evidence statuses are untouched. The implementation is a deletion of one predicate definition and its single bypass call, a catalog explanation correction, and a test replacement: the publisher-history expectations and the whole-archive WriteEvidence ratchet give way to ordinary synthetic projects that keep the useful generic controls.
Module responsibilities for this slice, around existing functions and artifacts — an explanatory map, not proposed new runtime classes:
Class: review engine, ledger evidence, declared scope, and engine path rules
classDiagram class ReviewEngine { runReview() } class WriteEvidenceScopeAudit { auditWriteEvidenceOutsideScope() } class RunLedger { WriteEvidence content paths } class ApprovedPlan { ObservedWriteScope files ObservedWriteScope globs } class EnginePathRules { CLI lifecycle artifacts Canonical candidate lock } class ReviewCatalog { Finding code and explanation } ReviewEngine --> RunLedger : reads evidence ReviewEngine --> WriteEvidenceScopeAudit : invokes WriteEvidenceScopeAudit --> ApprovedPlan : checks coverage WriteEvidenceScopeAudit --> EnginePathRules : preserves engine exceptions WriteEvidenceScopeAudit --> ReviewCatalog : reports generic finding

Alternatives.Alternative: Keep the `docs/plans/` exclusion. Rejected: it is a publisher-specific privilege inside a generic audit. It answers this repository's concurrency history by silently disarming the check for an arbitrary prefix, and its own Assumption admitted the hole. Consumers with a different roadmap prefix receive no such privilege, so the behavior is not the product's.

Narrow the exclusion to a fixed list of this repository's own files (the two measured `decisions.md`/`review.md` paths). Rejected: a one-off file list is a per-bundle allowlist by another name, it fails the F9.10.1 incentive test (authored by the party the audit constrains), and it still encodes publisher-local paths into generic runtime behavior.

Move the exclusion into configuration (a repository setting that suppresses selected path classes). Rejected: the brief forbids a configurable bypass, and a configuration switch would relocate the same privilege without answering why a consumer should need it. Genuine coordination is expressed by declaring the path in `ObservedWriteScope`, which already works.

Remove the lifecycle and canonical candidate-lock exclusions too, on the theory that any exclusion is a bypass. Rejected: the run ledger, the loose events, and the transient candidate lock are engine-owned recording and coordination artifacts, and this bundle preserves their existing exclusions. No engine rule is changed here; this slice removes only the publisher path privilege.

Also correct `C-CURRENT-VALIDATION-BOUNDARY-1-D8D7DF85`'s global archive validation and the XML parser comment exceptions in this bundle. Rejected as oversized and not independently verifiable: the design sequences those after the internal validation inputs are isolated, and the maintainer sanctioned small cohesive bundles with separate stage ratifications.

Flip the affected historical test expectations in place (expect the docs findings now, add a new archive multiset). Rejected: the tests would then encode the publisher archive as a compatibility population, which the active-development policy forbids, and a new historical multiset is the same coupling with reversed signs. Ordinary synthetic projects preserve the generic controls without binding the product to the archive.

DeferredDecisions.Decision: Generic archive-traversal restoration and removal of the XML parser's nine publisher-archive comment exceptions, after the internal validation inputs are isolated. Owner: the separate internal-validation-inputs cleanup bundle.

Other historical test consumers beyond the three affected blocks. Owner: the internal-validation-inputs bundle. This bundle requires no new historical conformance population at any stage; its final CI obligation retains the existing suite.

Skill/resource/template cleanup and portable-workflow teaching that drops publisher-corpus assumptions. Owner: separate authorized cleanup bundles. This bundle neither schedules nor asserts a defect on those surfaces, and assessment is not an implementation decision here.

README/roadmap policy repair, packaging, and release/version changes are outside this slice. Owner: separate authorized cleanup bundles; this bundle is version-neutral, leaves `README.md` and `examples/` unchanged, and asserts no defect there.

Scenario.Title: Sequence: declared-scope decision for a recorded WriteEvidence path
Scenario.Diagram: sequenceDiagram participant P as Approved consumer plan participant E as Executor participant C as ngrace CLI participant L as Run ledger participant A as WriteEvidence scope audit E->>C: Record attempt after project changes C->>L: Capture actual WriteEvidence paths C->>A: Review recorded paths A->>P: Read ObservedWriteScope files and globs alt Path is declared or a legitimate engine exception A-->>C: No scope finding else Path is undeclared, including docs/plans A-->>C: review.write-evidence-outside-scope end C-->>E: Report finding and audit status
Scenario.Steps: A comparable path is either covered by the plan's declared `File`/`Glob` or it is not. Active↔archive identity expansion for the reviewed change's own `.ngrace/changes/{active,archive}/<id>/...` bundle artifacts is a separate `.ngrace/` boundary, not an ordinary `docs/plans/` alias. Covered paths — including `docs/plans/` paths now that the prefix exemption is gone — produce no finding. Uncovered content paths produce `review.write-evidence-outside-scope` with severity `error`. The engine-owned lifecycle and exact canonical candidate-lock artifacts are preserved exclusions. This backs `AC-UNDECLARED-DOCS-PATH-RAISES` and `AC-DECLARED-DOCS-PASSES`.

Scenario.Title: Sequence: undeclared docs refusal, declared docs success, restoration
Scenario.Steps: On a clean committed throwaway project, record WriteEvidence naming a fixed `docs/plans/active/<X>/decisions.md` with a plan whose `ObservedWriteScope` does not cover it: the real CLI exits non-zero with exactly `review.write-evidence-outside-scope`. Then, in controlled disposable variants, change only the plan's `ObservedWriteScope` while keeping the recorded WriteEvidence path fixed — first add the exact `File`, then the matching `Glob` — and confirm the CLI exits 0 with no such finding; alternatively use separately declared fixtures. Restore each input byte-exactly after each probe. Then change the recorded WriteEvidence path to an undeclared `src/secret.ts` and confirm the same refusal. No historical red is manufactured and the old publisher archive is not the acceptance population.

Scenario.Title: Sequence: engine boundaries preserved
Scenario.Steps: Feed WriteEvidence naming `run.xml`, `run-ledger.xml`, and a `run/` event: no finding. Feed the exact canonical `.ngrace/changes/active/.candidate-<C-ID>.lock`: no finding. Feed each near miss in turn — archived location, extra nesting, another top-level directory, and a malformed id: every one raises. Feed an undeclared approved `spec.xml` or `plan.xml`: it raises. This backs `AC-PRESERVED-BOUNDARIES`.
